headline: California launches AI job loss tracker AI-related job cuts with monthly updates
summary: California's new portal tracks AI-related job losses by age, education, and more
details: California has launched a new portal to track AI-related job losses in the state. The tracker, developed by the office of Governor Gavin Newsom, the California Employment Development Department, and the California Policy Lab, uses Unemployment Insurance claims data and AI exposure measures to estimate job losses.

The tracker provides data on potential AI exposure by different groups, including age, education, gender, industry, race, and ethnicity, as well as by region. For instance, people in the 25 to 35 age group appear to be the most vulnerable to AI-related layoffs, with females more affected than males.

The tracker will be updated monthly and is intended to serve as an 'early warning system' for widespread job cuts due to artificial intelligence, allowing the government to proactively determine where interventions may be needed the most.

Can AI-related job losses be tracked and mitigated? California just launched a portal to monitor them

California has launched a new portal to track AI-related job losses in the state. The tracker, developed by the office of Governor Gavin Newsom, the California Employment Development Department, and the California Policy Lab, uses Unemployment Insurance claims data and AI exposure measures to estimate job losses.

The tracker provides data on potential AI exposure by different groups, including age, education, gender, industry, race, and ethnicity, as well as by region. For instance, people in the 25 to 35 age group appear to be the most vulnerable to AI-related layoffs, with females more affected than males.

The tracker will be updated monthly and is intended to serve as an 'early warning system' for widespread job cuts due to artificial intelligence, allowing the government to proactively determine where interventions may be needed the most.
